We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have identified possible building blocks: a brominated sulfonyl chloride (Brc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1) is buyable. Also an acryloyl anilide: C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1 (trans-? but it's an amide with phenyl). Also p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) is buyable.

Goal: final product is a sulfonamide linking two aryl rings: tolyl sulfonyl attached to an anilide phenyl with a trans-alkene linking to carbonyl amide attached to an aniline (anilide). Actually structure: tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached via sulfonamide to a phenyl ring (ring B) which is para-substituted with a trans-alkenyl carbonyl amide attached to an aniline (ring C). So we can think retrosynthesis:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide: target -> tolyl sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the second phenyl with the rest). So we need to make sulfonyl chloride from tolyl sulfonyl chloride (Brc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1) but we have bromine not methyl. Actually we need p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (CH3 on ring). But we have brominated sulfonyl chloride; we could do bromine to methyl via Suzuki? That adds cost. Better to find p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride directly buyable? Could check is_buyable for "Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1". Let's test.
